(#28)","ct_content":"
Travel outside of Arusha to a Masaai tribe and spend the entire day learning and experiencing  what it means to be a Masaai! <\/div>
This is a top rated tour, allowing tourists to see first hand how the tribe lives, eats, loves, and appreciates one another. <\/span><\/div>
Eye witness a sacrifice of a goat then assist the warrior prepare the meal for everyone to taste. It is a tradition to catch the blood from the goat and take a sip for good luck and prosper! <\/span><\/div>
Consumption is at your own discretion, but is encouraged and your guide will participate with you!<\/div>
Spend time with the grandparents, mamas, young adults, warriors and children.  Allow the tribe to dress you with their traditional clothing and beads. Then, watch them perform a dance for you! Learn the moves together and build friendships. <\/span><\/div>
The men of the tribe often move into the city areas in order to make money and provide for their families. While the children, elders, and women stay at home in the tribes, a method they use to make money is to make heaps of beaded jewelry to sell to tourists as they come visit.<\/span><\/div>","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"font-size":"14"}}}},"depth":6}]}]},{"id":42,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":42,"ct_parent":25,"selector":"div_block-42-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"100","text-align":"left","flex-direction":"row","display":"flex","gap":"30"},"nicename":"News Layer One","media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"flex-direction":"column","display":"flex","flex-reverse":"reverse"}}}},"depth":4,"children":[{"id":44,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":44,"ct_parent":42,"selector":"div_block-44-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"50"},"nicename":"TEXT","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"width":"100"}}}},"depth":5,"children":[{"id":45,"name":"ct_text_block","options":{"ct_id":45,"ct_parent":44,"selector":"text_block-45-150","original":{"font-size":"18","color":"#3d3d3d","text-align":"justify","-webkit-font-smoothing":"antialiased"},"nicename":"Text (#45)","ct_content":"One of the most profound experiences of the day is witnessing the sacred sacrifice of a goat, a ritual deeply embedded in Maasai culture. Under the guidance of skilled warriors, you’ll not only observe but also assist in preparing the meal for the entire tribe to enjoy. It is customary to collect the goat’s blood and take a sip—a symbolic act believed to bring good luck, strength, and prosperity. While the men of the tribe often venture into city areas to earn money for their families, the women, elders, and children remain in the villages, sustaining their traditions and way of life. 

One of the ways they support themselves is by creating and selling intricate beaded jewelry to visitors, a craft that reflects the beauty and resilience of their culture.

Ask the locals advice on the best experiences to have in Tanzania and how you can help to sustain the economy some more! \n\nFirst, you will stroll through the land and look at all of the magnificent banana plants. \nThen, you will be presented with a large tub filled with bottles of your treat!\nLastly, you will relax with your own taste of traditional Tanzanian alcohol while sharing conversation with Agape.

(#28)","ct_content":"<\/span>tep into history as you journey deep into an ancient cave once used by the Masasi tribe during times of war. This hidden underground refuge served as a vital stronghold, providing shelter and strategic defense against enemy tribes. As you descend a steep ladder into the depths of the cave, you’ll be transported back in time to an era of survival, resilience, and tactical warfare. Once inside, you’ll explore the narrow passages and learn about the incredible history of this secret hideout. Your guide will share fascinating stories of how the Masasi warriors lived, planned attacks, and protected their people from invaders.

The experience inside the cave lasts approximately 30 minutes, depending on the size of the group. Due to the confined space, only 3-5 people are allowed inside at a time to ensure a comfortable and immersive experience. Please be aware that this adventure requires a moderate level of physical ability, as you will need to climb down a steep ladder and navigate through low-ceiling passages, bending over for about 10-15 minutes. For this reason, the experience is  for individuals with back or neck injuries.

(#28)","ct_content":"
Travel outside of Arusha to a Masaai tribe and spend the entire day learning and experiencing  what it means to be a Masaai! <\/div>
This is a top rated tour, allowing tourists to see first hand how the tribe lives, eats, loves, and appreciates one another. <\/span><\/div>
Eye witness a sacrifice of a goat then assist the warrior prepare the meal for everyone to taste. It is a tradition to catch the blood from the goat and take a sip for good luck and prosper! <\/span><\/div>
Consumption is at your own discretion, but is encouraged and your guide will participate with you!<\/div>
Spend time with the grandparents, mamas, young adults, warriors and children.  Allow the tribe to dress you with their traditional clothing and beads. Then, watch them perform a dance for you! Learn the moves together and build friendships. <\/span><\/div>
The men of the tribe often move into the city areas in order to make money and provide for their families. While the children, elders, and women stay at home in the tribes, a method they use to make money is to make heaps of beaded jewelry to sell to tourists as they come visit.<\/span><\/div>","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"font-size":"14"}}}},"depth":6}]}]},{"id":42,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":42,"ct_parent":25,"selector":"div_block-42-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"100","text-align":"left","flex-direction":"row","display":"flex","gap":"30"},"nicename":"News Layer One","media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"flex-direction":"column","display":"flex","flex-reverse":"reverse"}}}},"depth":4,"children":[{"id":44,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":44,"ct_parent":42,"selector":"div_block-44-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"50"},"nicename":"TEXT","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"width":"100"}}}},"depth":5,"children":[{"id":45,"name":"ct_text_block","options":{"ct_id":45,"ct_parent":44,"selector":"text_block-45-150","original":{"font-size":"18","color":"#3d3d3d","text-align":"justify","-webkit-font-smoothing":"antialiased"},"nicename":"Text (#45)","ct_content":"One of the most profound experiences of the day is witnessing the sacred sacrifice of a goat, a ritual deeply embedded in Maasai culture. Under the guidance of skilled warriors, you’ll not only observe but also assist in preparing the meal for the entire tribe to enjoy. It is customary to collect the goat’s blood and take a sip—a symbolic act believed to bring good luck, strength, and prosperity. While the men of the tribe often venture into city areas to earn money for their families, the women, elders, and children remain in the villages, sustaining their traditions and way of life. 

One of the ways they support themselves is by creating and selling intricate beaded jewelry to visitors, a craft that reflects the beauty and resilience of their culture.

Indulge in two types of Tanzania alcohols and relax with a local, Agape! Enjoy bottled Banana Beer and a Banana Wine, homemade and delicious! Ask the locals advice on the best experiences to have in Tanzania and how you can help to sustain the economy some more! \n\nFirst, you will stroll through the land and look at all of the magnificent banana plants. \nThen, you will be presented with a large tub filled with bottles of your treat!\nLastly, you will relax with your own taste of traditional Tanzanian alcohol while sharing conversation with Agape. 

You will have 90 minutes to enjoy 2-3 servings of alcohol and then you may purchase a few bottles for your journey onwards!

(#28)","ct_content":"<\/span>tep into history as you journey deep into an ancient cave once used by the Masasi tribe during times of war. This hidden underground refuge served as a vital stronghold, providing shelter and strategic defense against enemy tribes. As you descend a steep ladder into the depths of the cave, you’ll be transported back in time to an era of survival, resilience, and tactical warfare. Once inside, you’ll explore the narrow passages and learn about the incredible history of this secret hideout. Your guide will share fascinating stories of how the Masasi warriors lived, planned attacks, and protected their people from invaders.

The experience inside the cave lasts approximately 30 minutes, depending on the size of the group. Due to the confined space, only 3-5 people are allowed inside at a time to ensure a comfortable and immersive experience. Please be aware that this adventure requires a moderate level of physical ability, as you will need to climb down a steep ladder and navigate through low-ceiling passages, bending over for about 10-15 minutes. For this reason, the experience is  for individuals with back or neck injuries.

(#28)","ct_content":"
Travel outside of Arusha to a Masaai tribe and spend the entire day learning and experiencing  what it means to be a Masaai! <\/div>
This is a top rated tour, allowing tourists to see first hand how the tribe lives, eats, loves, and appreciates one another. <\/span><\/div>
Eye witness a sacrifice of a goat then assist the warrior prepare the meal for everyone to taste. It is a tradition to catch the blood from the goat and take a sip for good luck and prosper! <\/span><\/div>
Consumption is at your own discretion, but is encouraged and your guide will participate with you!<\/div>
Spend time with the grandparents, mamas, young adults, warriors and children.  Allow the tribe to dress you with their traditional clothing and beads. Then, watch them perform a dance for you! Learn the moves together and build friendships. <\/span><\/div>
The men of the tribe often move into the city areas in order to make money and provide for their families. While the children, elders, and women stay at home in the tribes, a method they use to make money is to make heaps of beaded jewelry to sell to tourists as they come visit.<\/span><\/div>","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"font-size":"14"}}}},"depth":6}]}]},{"id":42,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":42,"ct_parent":25,"selector":"div_block-42-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"100","text-align":"left","flex-direction":"row","display":"flex","gap":"30"},"nicename":"News Layer One","media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"flex-direction":"column","display":"flex","flex-reverse":"reverse"}}}},"depth":4,"children":[{"id":44,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":44,"ct_parent":42,"selector":"div_block-44-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"50"},"nicename":"TEXT","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"width":"100"}}}},"depth":5,"children":[{"id":45,"name":"ct_text_block","options":{"ct_id":45,"ct_parent":44,"selector":"text_block-45-150","original":{"font-size":"18","color":"#3d3d3d","text-align":"justify","-webkit-font-smoothing":"antialiased"},"nicename":"Text (#45)","ct_content":"One of the most profound experiences of the day is witnessing the sacred sacrifice of a goat, a ritual deeply embedded in Maasai culture. Under the guidance of skilled warriors, you’ll not only observe but also assist in preparing the meal for the entire tribe to enjoy. It is customary to collect the goat’s blood and take a sip—a symbolic act believed to bring good luck, strength, and prosperity. While the men of the tribe often venture into city areas to earn money for their families, the women, elders, and children remain in the villages, sustaining their traditions and way of life. 

One of the ways they support themselves is by creating and selling intricate beaded jewelry to visitors, a craft that reflects the beauty and resilience of their culture.

(#28)","ct_content":"<\/span>tep into history as you journey deep into an ancient cave once used by the Masasi tribe during times of war. This hidden underground refuge served as a vital stronghold, providing shelter and strategic defense against enemy tribes. As you descend a steep ladder into the depths of the cave, you’ll be transported back in time to an era of survival, resilience, and tactical warfare. Once inside, you’ll explore the narrow passages and learn about the incredible history of this secret hideout. Your guide will share fascinating stories of how the Masasi warriors lived, planned attacks, and protected their people from invaders.

The experience inside the cave lasts approximately 30 minutes, depending on the size of the group. Due to the confined space, only 3-5 people are allowed inside at a time to ensure a comfortable and immersive experience. Please be aware that this adventure requires a moderate level of physical ability, as you will need to climb down a steep ladder and navigate through low-ceiling passages, bending over for about 10-15 minutes. For this reason, the experience is  for individuals with back or neck injuries.

(#28)","ct_content":"
Travel outside of Arusha to a Masaai tribe and spend the entire day learning and experiencing  what it means to be a Masaai! <\/div>
This is a top rated tour, allowing tourists to see first hand how the tribe lives, eats, loves, and appreciates one another. <\/span><\/div>
Eye witness a sacrifice of a goat then assist the warrior prepare the meal for everyone to taste. It is a tradition to catch the blood from the goat and take a sip for good luck and prosper! <\/span><\/div>
Consumption is at your own discretion, but is encouraged and your guide will participate with you!<\/div>
Spend time with the grandparents, mamas, young adults, warriors and children.  Allow the tribe to dress you with their traditional clothing and beads. Then, watch them perform a dance for you! Learn the moves together and build friendships. <\/span><\/div>
The men of the tribe often move into the city areas in order to make money and provide for their families. While the children, elders, and women stay at home in the tribes, a method they use to make money is to make heaps of beaded jewelry to sell to tourists as they come visit.<\/span><\/div>","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"font-size":"14"}}}},"depth":6}]}]},{"id":42,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":42,"ct_parent":25,"selector":"div_block-42-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"100","text-align":"left","flex-direction":"row","display":"flex","gap":"30"},"nicename":"News Layer One","media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"flex-direction":"column","display":"flex","flex-reverse":"reverse"}}}},"depth":4,"children":[{"id":44,"name":"ct_div_block","options":{"ct_id":44,"ct_parent":42,"selector":"div_block-44-150","original":{"width-unit":"%","width":"50"},"nicename":"TEXT","activeselector":false,"media":{"phone-portrait":{"original":{"width":"100"}}}},"depth":5,"children":[{"id":45,"name":"ct_text_block","options":{"ct_id":45,"ct_parent":44,"selector":"text_block-45-150","original":{"font-size":"18","color":"#3d3d3d","text-align":"justify","-webkit-font-smoothing":"antialiased"},"nicename":"Text (#45)","ct_content":"One of the most profound experiences of the day is witnessing the sacred sacrifice of a goat, a ritual deeply embedded in Maasai culture. Under the guidance of skilled warriors, you’ll not only observe but also assist in preparing the meal for the entire tribe to enjoy. It is customary to collect the goat’s blood and take a sip—a symbolic act believed to bring good luck, strength, and prosperity. While the men of the tribe often venture into city areas to earn money for their families, the women, elders, and children remain in the villages, sustaining their traditions and way of life. 

One of the ways they support themselves is by creating and selling intricate beaded jewelry to visitors, a craft that reflects the beauty and resilience of their culture.

Indulge in two types of Tanzania alcohols and relax with a local, Agape! Enjoy bottled Banana Beer and a Banana Wine, homemade and delicious! Sit in a “shack” and share stories about each other’s cultures. Ask the locals advice on the best experiences to have in Tanzania and how you can help to sustain the economy some more! \n\nFirst, you will stroll through the land and look at all of the magnificent banana plants. \nThen, you will be presented with a large tub filled with bottles of your treat!\nLastly, you will relax with your own taste of traditional Tanzanian alcohol while sharing conversation with Agape. 

You will have 90 minutes to enjoy 2-3 servings of alcohol and then you may purchase a few bottles for your journey onwards!

(#28)","ct_content":"<\/span>tep into history as you journey deep into an ancient cave once used by the Masasi tribe during times of war. This hidden underground refuge served as a vital stronghold, providing shelter and strategic defense against enemy tribes. As you descend a steep ladder into the depths of the cave, you’ll be transported back in time to an era of survival, resilience, and tactical warfare. Once inside, you’ll explore the narrow passages and learn about the incredible history of this secret hideout. Your guide will share fascinating stories of how the Masasi warriors lived, planned attacks, and protected their people from invaders.

The experience inside the cave lasts approximately 30 minutes, depending on the size of the group. Due to the confined space, only 3-5 people are allowed inside at a time to ensure a comfortable and immersive experience. Please be aware that this adventure requires a moderate level of physical ability, as you will need to climb down a steep ladder and navigate through low-ceiling passages, bending over for about 10-15 minutes. For this reason, the experience is  for individuals with back or neck injuries.

Embark on a thrilling 10-day safari through Tanzania and Kenya, starting with Tarangire National Park’s iconic elephant herds. Explore the Ngorongoro Crater, Serengeti, and Lake Victoria before venturing into the Masai Mara, home to the Big Five and diverse wildlife. Experience game drives, cultural encounters, and stunning landscapes while staying in luxury lodges and tented camps throughout the journey.

Distance approx. 150 km; driving time approx. 2-3 hours After a short briefing in the morning, your safari will set off towards the Tarangire National Park. This park with its savannah, seasonal swamps and the life-giving Tarangire River is home to huge elephant herds – literally hundreds of animals. Animals gather at the river and besides elephants you should see mongoose, giraffes, bushbucks, hartebeests, dik-diks, waterbucks, warthogs and reedbucks all year round. After an extensive game drive, you will leave the park in the late afternoon and head to the Lake Burunge Baobab Tented Lodge where you will spend the night.
Transport in a 4x4 safari vehicle (change of vehicle at the border)

Distance approx. 120 km; driving time approx. 2 hours After a delicious breakfast, you return to Tarangire National Park for another game drive. Since the park is so rich in wildlife, you are sure to spot animals you didn’t see yesterday. Your guide will share his in-depth knowledge about flora and fauna of the region with you and you may be surprised how much you have seen and learned on only your second day of safari. The Baobab trees scattered across the park make Tarangire one of the most scenic regions on the Northern Circuit. After an extensive game drive, you will travel to Karatu in the Ngorongoro highlands. After your arrival, there might be time for an optional walk in the coffee plantations. You will spend the night at one of the three beautifully located Tanganyika Wilderness Adventure Lodges.

Distance approx. 170 km; driving time approx. 4-6 hours You will have breakfast at dawn before the 4×4 safari vehicle takes you to the crater rim from where you descend into the crater on an adventurous and steep trail. Down here in the crater you have the possibility of seeing all the animals that can be found in the East African savannah including the Big Five – lion, elephant, buffalo, rhino and leopard. The Ngorongoro Crater is also one of the best places to see the magnificent but almost extinct black rhino. After an extensive game drive, you will exit the crater in the early afternoon. The journey then continues to the plains of the Serengeti National Park – the most famous park in Tanzania and where the biggest animal migration in the world takes place. Hundred thousand of wildebeests and zebras cross the border from the Serengeti to the Masai Mara in Kenya in search of fresh grass and water, with hungry predators following close behind. You will spend the night at the Kati Kati Tented Camp in the central Serengeti.

Rise and shine! Up at the crack of dawn, you will be able to see the sunrise over the Serengeti before you join an early morning game drive. Upon your return to the camp, a hearty breakfast awaits. Adventurous guests may choose to experience the Serengeti from the sky and join a hot-air balloon ride followed by a champagne breakfast in the bush. This activity is not included in the tour price and needs to be booked in advance. Guests interested in visiting the visitor Centre, are also able to do so. In the afternoon you will enjoy another game drive before returning to the Kati Kati Tented Camp for dinner and overnight

Distance approx. 180 km; driving time approx. 4-5 hours After an early start, you will travel through the Serengeti National Park and on your way out of the park you might spot animals you haven’t seen yet. After leaving the park, the safari continues to Lake Victoria, the largest lake in Africa and the second largest in the world. The area around Lake Victoria is the most fertile and densely populated region in Tanzania. Here at Lake Victoria, you will have the chance to see another side of Tanzania. Away from the tourists and the masses, you will experience the lives of the local people. You can take a walk along the lake shore and watch fishermen at work – an experience unavailable on the usual tourist routes. The night will be spent at the Speke Bay Lodge.
Lake Victoria, Tanzania – Masai Mara Area, Kenya

Distance approx. 270 km; driving time approx. 8-9 hours After breakfast you will join the local fishermen and a guide on a canoe trip on Lake Victoria. You will see how the locals catch fish the traditional way and admire the previous night’s catch. After your fishing excursion you will set off on the longest journey of your safari – the trip to the Masai Mara. The road towards the Kenyan border is a long and adventurous one, but it should be worth it as the “Mara” is reputed to have the highest lion population of all reserves in Africa. Other large cats like leopards and cheetahs also live here and can be spotted all year round, as their sightings are not dependent upon the seasons or the migration. You will overnight in luxury tents at the Mara West Camp on the outskirts of the Masai Mara Game Reserve.
Masai Mara Game Reserve Game drives

You can look forward to a day dedicated to safari and game viewing. On extensive game drives in your 4×4 safari vehicle you will explore the Mara Triangle, located in the north-western part of the Masai Mara. Far stretching grassland plains, dotted by acacia forests, dominate the landscape. You will take a trip to the Mara River, the greatest hurdle for the wildebeests and zebras on their yearly trek. At the end of October and the beginning of November, an incredible scene is set when the river swells to almost bursting levels and tens of thousands of animals prepare to cross it, knowing that possible death awaits them – as crocodiles are hiding just below the water’s surface. It can be a gruesome sight. At other times of the year, hippos, hungry crocodiles, and other animals can also be seen near the river. In the late afternoon, as the shadows start to grow longer, you return to your accommodation and spend another night at the Mara West Camp.
Masai Mara Game Reserve Game drives

The following two days will be spent on game drives in the Masai Mara Game Reserve. Together with your guide you can search for the Big Five. You are in no rush, so you have enough time to enjoy all the wonderful moments which can make your safari a magical experience. The Mara is home to many other interesting animals too, such as Thomson’s and Grant’s gazelles, elands, and Coke’s hartebeests. Not often seen outside Kenya are the Masai giraffe, roan antelope and the nocturnal bat-eared fox. The reserve also has over 470 bird species including about 60 raptor species. You will spend two nights at the Mara Legends Camp inside the Masai Mara Game Reserve

Distance approx. 270 km; driving time approx. 6-7 hours After breakfast you will leave the bush for Nairobi, Kenya’s bustling and often chaotic capital. You will arrive in the late afternoon and depending on the rest of your travel plans, you will be taken to your hotel in the city centre or directly to the airport.
Professional, English-speaking guide (change of guide at the border)
9 nights’ stay in lodges and tented camps
Activities and transfers as per itinerary

Experience an unforgettable 8-day safari adventure in Kenya, exploring Nairobi National Park, the Maasai Mara, Lake Nakuru, and Amboseli National Park. Enjoy thrilling game drives, wildlife encounters, and cultural visits to iconic sites like the David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage and Giraffe Center. Conclude with a scenic journey through Kenya's diverse landscapes and a visit to the Amboseli’s majestic elephants.
Your safari guide will pick you up from the airport and transfer you to your hotel 67 for overnight

You will be picked up from your hotel in the morning and taken to Nairobi National Park where you will go on a morning game drive until 10:30 am. and you will go to David Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage for the feeding program between 11:00 and 12:00 pm. You will then head to the Giraffe Center where you will be able to feed the Rothchild Giraffes. You will then head for lunch (own expense) at one of Karen's restaurants. After lunch, you will visit the Karen Blixen Museum. You will then be driven back to 67 Hotel for dinner and overnight.

Your tour begins with a 7:30 am pick up from Ibis Styles and the drive to Maasai Mara. This trip will take approximately 5 to 6.5 hours with a scenic stop at the Great Rift Valley. You will arrive in Maasai Mara shortly after midday and check in at Enkorok Mara/camp, enjoy a hot lunch and then depart for an afternoon game drive. After the game drive, we will return to the lodge/camp to arrive around 6:00 pm, freshen up and enjoy a freshly prepared dinner. We will spend the night at Enkorok Mara Camp.

Today's itinerary is flexible and you can talk to your guide the night before and plan today's program. After breakfast, head out with your packed lunch and return to camp in the afternoon around 4:00 pm. Or you can depart at 6:00 am on a morning game drive (this is the best time to see the animals and a good chance to witness the hunt/kill). Later, return to the lodge for breakfast and some relaxation and head out on an afternoon game drive with packed lunch. You will stop at a picnic spot for packed lunch and then head out on a game drive until the park is closed. Around 6:00 pm you will return to Enkorok for dinner and overnight.
Depart Maasai Mara and head to Lake Nakuru. Arrive in time for lunch and afternoon game drive, dinner and overnight in Sopa forest.
Early morning departure after breakfast and drive through Nairobi to the Amboseli National Park. Lunch at Sentrim Camp, Amboseli afternoon game drive and return to camp.
You can go on a full day game drive in Amboseli. Dinner and overnight at Sentrim Amboseli
We will depart after breakfast and be dropped off at airport

Embark on a 9-day Kenya Wildlife Photography Safari, capturing stunning landscapes and wildlife from Amboseli to Masai Mara. Enjoy game drives, chasing the Big 5, and iconic species like elephants, rhinos, and flamingos, while staying at top lodges like Amboseli Serena and Loyk Mara Camp. This all-inclusive adventure offers expert guidance, exclusive 4x4 transport, and immersive experiences in Kenya's most scenic wildlife parks.

Leave Nairobi Early in the morning and head south with several stops on the way for landscapes and coffee breaks. We arrive in time for lunch at Amboseli Serena. After relaxing from the 4 to 5 hour drive we embark on our first photography game drive looking for elephants and any interesting creative setup. We end the evening with silhouette photography as the sun goes down
Full Days at Amboseli National Park

We leave the lodge with packed breakfast every day, chasing the sunset and playing with the elements, that is, light dust and the wildlife. We return to camp for lunch and head out again in the evening as the sun’s temperatures begin to cool and the light gets better for capturing the shots. Overnight and all meals at Amboseli Serena
Amboseli National Park to Lake Nakuru National Park

We leave after breakfast and proceed to Lake Nakuru national park. After approximately 7hrs we arrive and start our game drive at this awe inspiring park. We search for both the black and white rhinos, lions antelopes, visit the shore lines for the flamingos and pelicans. Dinner and lunch will be at the Lake Nakuru Sopa lodge.
Lake Nakuru National Park to Masai Mara

After breakfast we have a short drive to maximize the morning light and later drive to the Masai Mara Game Reserve as you enjoy the scenic views of the Great Rift Valley - Masai Mara game reserve is the northern part of the Serengeti, one of Kenya's most favoured game-viewing areas. The reserve covers 700 square miles of magnificent wilderness. It is the Africa of the imagination; endless reaches of acacia-dotted grasslands studded with hazy hills. Afternoon game drive to see the sundowner as you trail the Big 5 i.e. Lions in large prides, Elephants, buffalos, zebras and numerous plain game. Dinner and overnight stay at loyk Mara Camp. Meal plan: Lunch, Dinner
Full Days at Masai Mara National Reserve

Full days spent exploring the park in search of the big 5/other predators. Optional hot air balloon safari can be arranged at an extra cost of US$ 450 per person. Dinner and overnight at loyk Mara Camp. The Mara offers wildlife in such variety and abundance that it is difficult to believe: over 450 species of animals have been recorded here. You will easily see lions, rhinos, hippos, crocodiles, giraffe, wildebeests, zebras, buffalo, warthogs, hyenas, jackals, wild dogs, buffalo, leopard, many kinds of antelopes and elephant. It is in the Mara that perhaps the most spectacular event of the natural world takes place. This is the annual migration of millions of wildebeest and zebra from the Serengeti (Tanzania) in search of water and pasture. Following on their heels are the predators of the savanna- lion, cheetah, wild dog, jackal, hyena and vultures
After a morning game drive we will head back to Nairobi arriving by early evening.
Transport in a 4x4 land cruiser special for game viewing and photography
Full board accommodation whilst on safari
All park entrance fees to include government taxes
Service of an English-speaking professional driver/guide
All game drives as detailed in the itinerary
Hotel accommodations in Nairobi before and after the safari

item.title: Arusha Charity Programme
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Arusha Charity Programme: Making a Difference in Local Communities
Overview
The Arusha Charity Programme is a community-driven initiative dedicated to empowering local communities in and around Arusha, Tanzania. This program focuses on education, healthcare, environmental conservation, and social welfare, aiming to uplift underprivileged families and provide sustainable opportunities for growth. By partnering with local organizations, volunteers, and donors, the programme ensures that vulnerable communities receive the support they need to thrive.

Key Focus Areas

  1. Education Support
    The Arusha Charity Programme works to improve access to quality education for children from low-income families. This includes:

Providing school supplies, uniforms, and books.
Sponsoring tuition fees for students in need.
Supporting local schools with infrastructure development and learning materials.

  1. Healthcare Initiatives
    Ensuring access to basic healthcare services is a crucial part of the programme. Activities include:

Organizing free medical camps for underserved communities.
Providing essential medications and medical supplies to local clinics.
Promoting health education and awareness, focusing on hygiene, nutrition, and disease prevention.

  1. Environmental Conservation
    The programme is committed to preserving Tanzania’s natural beauty and resources through:

Tree-planting campaigns to combat deforestation.
Community clean-up drives to promote environmental sustainability.
Educating locals on eco-friendly practices and waste management.

  1. Empowering Women and Youth
    The programme supports women and young people by:

Offering vocational training and entrepreneurship workshops.
Providing microloans and financial support for small businesses.
Encouraging leadership and community engagement opportunities.
How You Can Get Involved
Whether you're a volunteer, donor, or traveler, you can make a difference by:

Donating to support education, healthcare, and environmental projects.
Volunteering your time and skills to assist local initiatives.
Participating in community outreach programs during your visit to Arusha.
Join us in creating lasting change and supporting the Arusha Charity Programme to build a better future for all!

item.title: Embark on a Wildlife Safari
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Embark on a Wildlife Safari in Tanzania
Tanzania is a land of untamed beauty, where the wilderness comes alive with breathtaking landscapes and abundant wildlife. For adventure seekers and nature lovers, a safari in Tanzania offers an unrivaled experience, with its world-famous national parks teeming with diverse animal species.

Serengeti National Park – Witness the Great Migration
One of the most spectacular wildlife experiences in the world takes place in Serengeti National Park. Renowned for its annual Great Migration, millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles traverse the vast plains in search of fresh grazing lands, creating a dramatic display of survival and instinct. Visitors can witness this extraordinary event and marvel at the predators, including lions, cheetahs, and crocodiles, that follow the herds in search of their next meal. The Serengeti is a dream destination for photographers and wildlife enthusiasts alike.

Ngorongoro Conservation Area – A Natural Wildlife Haven
Just south of the Serengeti lies the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, home to the famous Ngorongoro Crater. This massive volcanic caldera is often referred to as the "Eighth Wonder of the World" due to its incredible density of wildlife. Within its 260 square kilometers, visitors can spot the Big Five—lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos—alongside thousands of wildebeest, zebras, and hippos. The lush landscapes and permanent water sources make this a perfect sanctuary for animals throughout the year.

Tarangire National Park – The Land of Giants
Tarangire National Park is famous for its majestic baobab trees and large herds of elephants that roam freely across the park’s savannah. This park is home to one of the highest concentrations of wildlife outside the Serengeti ecosystem. Visitors can encounter giraffes, elands, impalas, and even rare species such as the fringe-eared oryx and greater kudu. Tarangire also boasts a rich birdlife, with over 500 species recorded, making it a paradise for birdwatchers.

Lake Manyara National Park – The Kingdom of Tree-Climbing Lions
Nestled at the base of the Great Rift Valley, Lake Manyara National Park is a hidden gem known for its tree-climbing lions—a rare and fascinating behavior not commonly seen elsewhere. The park also features lush groundwater forests, open grasslands, and the vast Lake Manyara itself, which attracts thousands of flamingos and other water birds. Hippos, baboons, and giraffes are frequently spotted, making this park a diverse and rewarding safari destination.

Why Choose Tanzania for Your Safari?
A Tanzanian safari is more than just a wildlife tour—it’s an unforgettable journey into nature’s wonders. With an array of breathtaking landscapes and an unmatched variety of animal species, every game drive promises a new and thrilling experience. Whether it’s witnessing the Great Migration in the Serengeti, exploring the depths of the Ngorongoro Crater, or marveling at the unique wildlife of Tarangire and Lake Manyara, Tanzania offers an adventure like no other.

item.title: Conquer the Roof of Africa
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Conquer the Roof of Africa: A Guide to Climbing Mount Kilimanjaro
Towering at 5,895 meters (19,341 feet) above sea level, Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest peak in Africa and the tallest freestanding mountain in the world. This iconic mountain, located in Tanzania, draws thousands of climbers annually, each seeking the challenge and reward of reaching its Uhuru Peak.

For adventure seekers, summiting Kilimanjaro is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Unlike other high-altitude climbs that require technical mountaineering skills, Kilimanjaro is a non-technical climb, meaning you don’t need ropes or specialized climbing equipment. However, the journey to the top requires physical endurance, mental resilience, and proper acclimatization.

Choosing Your Climbing Route
There are several routes leading to the summit, each offering a unique experience. One of the most well-known paths is the Marangu Route, often called the “Coca-Cola Route.”

The Marangu Route: The Classic Path
The Marangu Route is one of the most popular and accessible routes for climbers attempting to reach the summit. It is the only route with hut accommodations, making it a preferred choice for those who want more comfort during their trek.

Key Features of the Marangu Route
Accommodation: Unlike other routes where climbers camp in tents, Marangu offers huts with dormitory-style beds, dining halls, and basic toilets. These huts provide some protection against the elements, especially during rainy conditions.
Duration: The trek typically takes 5 to 6 days, with an optional acclimatization day at Horombo Hut to help climbers adjust to the altitude.
Scenery: The route passes through diverse landscapes, starting from lush rainforests and transitioning into moorlands, alpine deserts, and finally the snowy summit.
Difficulty Level: While it is considered one of the easier routes in terms of terrain, its major challenge is acclimatization. The relatively quick ascent means less time for the body to adapt to high altitudes, increasing the risk of altitude sickness.
Marangu Route Itinerary


Day 1: Marangu Gate (1,860m) to Mandara Hut (2,700m)

A scenic trek through dense rainforest, home to blue monkeys and exotic bird species.
Distance: 8 km (5 miles) | Duration: 4-5 hours.


Day 2: Mandara Hut to Horombo Hut (3,720m)

The landscape transitions from rainforest to open moorland with giant lobelias and senecios.
Distance: 12 km (7.5 miles) | Duration: 6-8 hours.


Day 3: Horombo Hut to Kibo Hut (4,703m)

A challenging day as you enter the alpine desert with dramatic views of Mawenzi and Kibo peaks.
Distance: 10 km (6 miles) | Duration: 6-8 hours.


Day 4: Kibo Hut to Uhuru Peak (5,895m) & descent to Horombo Hut

A midnight start to the summit attempt via Gilman’s Point (5,685m) before reaching Uhuru Peak—the highest point in Africa.
A rewarding but demanding climb in freezing temperatures.
After reaching the summit, descent back to Horombo Hut for rest.
Distance: 22 km (14 miles) | Duration: 10-16 hours.


Day 5: Horombo Hut to Marangu Gate

The final descent back through the rainforest to the starting point.
Distance: 20 km (12.5 miles) | Duration: 5-7 hours.
Challenges of the Marangu Route
While the Marangu Route is often considered easier in terms of terrain, it presents a higher risk of altitude sickness because of its rapid ascent. Unlike routes like Lemosho or Machame, which allow more time for gradual acclimatization, Marangu’s 5-6 day itinerary requires climbers to adjust quickly to the high altitude.

To increase the chances of a successful summit, climbers should:
✔ Take an extra acclimatization day at Horombo Hut.
✔ Hike at a slow and steady pace ("Pole Pole" in Swahili).
✔ Stay hydrated and eat well.
✔ Watch for symptoms of altitude sickness, such as headaches, dizziness, and nausea.

Why Climb Kilimanjaro?
Reaching the summit of Kilimanjaro is an achievement like no other. Standing atop Uhuru Peak at sunrise, gazing at the endless clouds and glaciers below, is a moment of pure triumph. The journey challenges both the body and mind, leaving climbers with unforgettable memories and a profound sense of accomplishment.

Are you ready to take on the challenge and conquer the Roof of Africa? Let Ndewedo Tours guide you on this incredible adventure! 🚀🏔

item.title: Unwind on Zanzibar's beaches
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
A Perfect Island Escape
After days of thrilling safaris or mountain adventures, Zanzibar offers the perfect retreat with its pristine beaches, turquoise waters, and rich cultural heritage. This breathtaking archipelago, located off Tanzania’s coast, is renowned for its white sandy beaches, crystal-clear waters, and historic charm. Whether you seek relaxation, exploration, or adventure, Zanzibar provides an unforgettable island getaway.

Unwind on Zanzibar’s World-Class Beaches
Zanzibar is home to some of the most stunning beaches in the world, each offering a unique experience.

Nungwi Beach – Located in the north, Nungwi is famous for its powdery white sand, vibrant nightlife, and breathtaking sunsets. Unlike many beaches in Zanzibar, Nungwi experiences minimal tidal changes, making it ideal for swimming at any time of the day.


Kendwa Beach – Just south of Nungwi, Kendwa boasts calm, shallow waters and a lively beach scene with full-moon parties and beachfront resorts. It’s perfect for those who want to mix relaxation with social activities.


Paje Beach – A haven for kite surfers and adventure seekers, Paje features strong ocean breezes, making it the best spot for watersports like windsurfing and paddleboarding.
Jambiani Beach – For a more authentic and quiet retreat, Jambiani offers a peaceful fishing village atmosphere with swaying palm trees and fewer tourists. It’s an ideal location for those looking to experience local culture and unspoiled nature.


Explore the Historic Stone Town
Beyond its beaches, Zanzibar’s Stone Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, offers a deep dive into the island’s rich history and vibrant culture. The town’s narrow, winding alleys are lined with intricately carved doors, bustling markets, and centuries-old buildings that reflect the island’s Swahili, Arab, Indian, and European influences.

Must-Visit Attractions in Stone Town:
The House of Wonders (Beit-al-Ajaib) – Once the sultan’s palace, this historic building showcases Zanzibar’s cultural heritage.
Forodhani Gardens – A lively waterfront night market offering fresh seafood, Zanzibar pizzas, and local delicacies.
Old Fort – A 17th-century fortress where visitors can explore ruins, shop for crafts, and enjoy cultural performances.
Freddie Mercury’s House – The birthplace of the legendary Queen vocalist, offering insight into his early life.
Indulge in Zanzibar’s Rich Culinary Scene
Zanzibar is known as the “Spice Island”, and its cuisine is a blend of African, Arab, Indian, and European flavors. Some must-try dishes include:

Zanzibar Pilau – A spiced rice dish infused with cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom.
Seafood Platters – Freshly caught fish, lobster, prawns, and octopus grilled to perfection.
Urojo (Zanzibar Mix) – A flavorful street food soup made with potatoes, crispy bhajias, coconut, and tangy mango.
Sugarcane Juice & Spice Tea – Refreshing drinks infused with local spices.
Activities for Every Traveler
For those seeking adventure beyond the beach, Zanzibar offers a range of exciting activities:

Snorkeling & Diving – Explore the vibrant coral reefs of Mnemba Atoll and Chumbe Island Marine Park.
Dhow Cruises – Sail along the coast in a traditional wooden dhow, enjoying a romantic sunset or a full-day island-hopping experience.
Jozani Forest Tour – Discover the endangered Zanzibar Red Colobus Monkeys, unique to the island.
Prison Island Tour – Visit the historic Changuu Island, home to giant Aldabra tortoises and a former slave prison.
Why Visit Zanzibar?
Whether you dream of lounging on sun-drenched shores, exploring centuries-old streets, or indulging in exotic flavors, Zanzibar offers the ultimate tropical escape. The island’s perfect blend of relaxation, history, and adventure makes it an ideal destination for honeymooners, families, and solo travelers alike.

Let Ndewedo Tours guide you to an unforgettable Zanzibar experience!

item.title: Explore Tanzania's traditions
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Immerse Yourself in Cultural Richness
Tanzania’s diverse cultures and traditions are as captivating as its landscapes. Engaging with local communities, especially the Maasai, provides a unique opportunity to experience traditions that have been preserved for generations. Through cultural tourism programs, travelers can interact with indigenous groups, learn about their way of life, and contribute to local economic growth and heritage preservation.

Discover the Maasai Way of Life
The Maasai people, known for their colorful attire, intricate beadwork, and deep-rooted customs, are among Tanzania’s most recognized ethnic groups. A visit to a traditional Maasai village (boma) offers an immersive experience in their:

Daily routines – Herding cattle, building traditional homes, and preparing meals.
Dance and music – Witness the iconic Adumu (jumping dance), performed during celebrations and rites of passage.
Storytelling and traditions – Learn about Maasai myths, ancestral wisdom, and their connection to nature.
Other Cultural Experiences in Tanzania

  1. Hadzabe & Datoga Tribes in Lake Eyasi
    The Hadzabe, one of Africa’s last hunter-gatherer tribes, showcase a traditional way of life that has remained unchanged for centuries. Visitors can join them on hunting expeditions and learn about foraging techniques.
    The Datoga, known for their blacksmithing skills, craft jewelry, arrowheads, and tools using ancient metalworking techniques.
  2. Chagga Culture on Mount Kilimanjaro’s Slopes
    The Chagga people, who inhabit the foothills of Mount Kilimanjaro, are known for their banana farming, coffee cultivation, and underground cave dwellings. A visit includes:

Touring local coffee farms and participating in coffee-making processes.
Exploring Chagga caves, which were once used as hideouts during tribal conflicts.
Learning about traditional brewing techniques and tasting local banana beer.

  1. Zanzibar’s Swahili Heritage
    Zanzibar’s culture is a blend of African, Arab, Indian, and European influences. Visitors can explore:

Stone Town’s historic sites, including old palaces and spice markets.
Swahili cuisine, featuring dishes like pilau rice, seafood curries, and chapati.
Traditional Taarab music, a melodic fusion of Arabic and African rhythms.
Why Cultural Tourism Matters
Participating in cultural experiences not only enriches a traveler’s journey but also:

Supports local communities, providing income for artisans, guides, and families.
Preserves indigenous traditions, ensuring that centuries-old customs continue for future generations.
Promotes responsible tourism, fostering deeper understanding and respect for Tanzania’s diverse cultures.
Immerse yourself in Tanzania’s rich cultural heritage and create meaningful connections with its people!

item.title: Tanzania's Hidden Gems
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Off-the-Beaten-Path Adventures
While Tanzania is famous for its iconic destinations like the Serengeti and Mount Kilimanjaro, there are many lesser-known but equally captivating places waiting to be explored. From remote islands to serene lakes and hidden wildlife reserves, Tanzania’s hidden gems offer unique adventures for those seeking a more authentic and peaceful experience.

  1. Mafia Island – A Tranquil Beach Escape
    Located off the southern coast of Tanzania, Mafia Island is a hidden paradise for those looking to escape the crowds. Known for its pristine beaches, vibrant coral reefs, and rich marine life, Mafia is ideal for snorkeling, diving, and relaxing by the beach. The island is part of the Mafia Island Marine Park, where visitors can swim with whale sharks or explore the underwater world of colorful fish and coral gardens.
  2. Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani – A Historical Journey
    For history buffs, the Kilwa Kisiwani ruins are a fascinating, yet often overlooked, destination. Located on an island off the southern coast of Tanzania, the ruins are remnants of the once-thriving Swahili trading town. Kilwa Kisiwani was a center for trade in gold, ivory, and slaves between the 9th and 16th centuries and was once a powerful city-state. The ancient structures, including the Sultans’ palaces and mosques, offer a glimpse into Tanzania’s rich cultural and historical past.
  3. Selous Game Reserve – Untamed Wilderness
    While the Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater are popular wildlife destinations, Selous Game Reserve (now Nyerere National Park) offers an equally thrilling experience with far fewer tourists. As one of the largest game reserves in Africa, Selous is home to a diverse range of wildlife, including lions, elephants, giraffes, and buffaloes, as well as endangered species like the African wild dog. Visitors can enjoy boat safaris along the Rufiji River, walking safaris, or traditional game drives in an area that remains largely untamed.
  4. Lake Natron – A Breathtaking Salt Lake
    For a truly otherworldly experience, visit Lake Natron, located in northern Tanzania near the Kenyan border. Known for its striking red and orange hues, the lake is fed by hot springs and volcanic minerals, giving it a surreal, otherworldly appearance. The lake is also a breeding ground for lesser flamingos, providing a unique opportunity to witness thousands of these beautiful birds up close. The surrounding Mount Oldonyo Lengai, an active volcano, adds to the area’s dramatic landscape.
  5. Kitulo National Park – Tanzania’s "Garden of God"
    Known as the “Garden of God,” Kitulo National Park is a hidden gem for nature lovers and flower enthusiasts. Situated on the southern highlands, Kitulo is famous for its lush meadows, which are filled with wildflowers and orchids in full bloom during the rainy season. This biodiversity hotspot is also home to various species of birds, including the rare blue swallow. Kitulo offers a peaceful retreat, perfect for those seeking to immerse themselves in Tanzania’s natural beauty.
  6. Saadani National Park – Where the Ocean Meets the Wild
    For a unique wildlife experience, visit Saadani National Park, the only park in Tanzania that combines both savannah and coastal ecosystems. Located along the Indian Ocean, Saadani offers a rare opportunity to spot wildlife like elephants, lions, and leopards, while enjoying the pristine beaches and coastal scenery. Visitors can enjoy both game drives and beach walks, all while being serenaded by the sounds of the ocean.

Why Explore Tanzania's Hidden Gems?
Authenticity: Explore less touristy destinations and enjoy a more authentic, peaceful experience.


Unique Landscapes: From red salt lakes to lush meadows, Tanzania’s hidden gems offer stunning landscapes beyond the typical safari.


Adventure Awaits: Whether you’re into diving with whale sharks, exploring ancient ruins, or trekking in remote wilderness, there’s something for every adventurer.
Support Local Communities: Visiting lesser-known destinations often supports local economies and contributes to conservation efforts.


Tanzania is full of hidden treasures waiting to be discovered. Whether you’re a seasoned traveler or a first-time visitor, the country’s lesser-known destinations offer unique and unforgettable experiences. Let Ndewedo Tours guide you off the beaten path to explore the true magic of Tanzania.

item.title: Terms & Conditions
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Ndewedo Tours and Safari Refund Policy

At Ndewedo Tours and Safari, we strive to provide unforgettable experiences. We understand that plans can change, and we’ve designed this refund policy to be clear, fair, and considerate for all guests.

1. Booking Cancellations

  • Cancellations 60 days or more before departure:
    Full refund minus a 10% administrative fee.
  • Cancellations 30–59 days before departure:
    50% refund of the total tour price.
  • Cancellations less than 30 days before departure:
    No refund.

Some tours, especially those involving special permits (e.g., gorilla trekking), may be non-refundable once booked due to third-party restrictions.

2. No-Show Policy

Guests who fail to arrive at the scheduled meeting point or departure time without prior notice will not be eligible for a refund.

3. Changes and Rescheduling

  • Changes to travel dates are allowed subject to availability and must be requested at least 30 days before departure.
  • Additional costs (e.g., hotel or transport changes) may apply and will be communicated prior to confirmation.

4. Cancellations by Ndewedo Tours and Safari

  • If we must cancel a trip due to unforeseen circumstances (e.g., weather, safety concerns, insufficient participants), guests will be offered:
    • A full refund, or
    • The option to reschedule or apply the payment to a future tour.

Ndewedo Tours and Safari is not responsible for non-refundable expenses (e.g., flights, visas) not booked through us.

5. Refund Process

  • Refund requests must be made in writing via email to [your company email].
  • Approved refunds will be processed within 14 business days using the original payment method.
  • Any bank or transfer fees are the responsibility of the guest.

6. Travel Insurance

We strongly recommend that all guests purchase comprehensive travel insurance to cover unexpected cancellations, medical emergencies, or other travel disruptions.

item.title: Refund Policy
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.content:encoded:
Refund Policy for Ndewedo Tours and Safari

At Ndewedo Tours and Safari, we are committed to providing you with memorable and enjoyable travel experiences. However, we understand that circumstances can change. This Refund Policy outlines our procedures and conditions regarding refunds for bookings made with us.

By booking a tour, safari, or other travel services with Ndewedo Tours and Safari, you agree to the terms of this Refund Policy.

1. Refund Eligibility

Refunds are only applicable under the following conditions:

  • You cancel your booking in accordance with the cancellation policy outlined at the time of booking.
  • You are unable to travel due to unforeseen events that are covered by insurance or qualify for a refund.
  • Ndewedo Tours and Safari fails to provide the services as outlined in your booking (e.g., a significant change to the itinerary, accommodation, or transportation that you do not accept).

2. Refund Process

To request a refund, the Group Leader (for group bookings) or the individual traveler must:

  • Contact us by email or phone as soon as possible.
  • Provide your booking reference number and the details of the cancellation request.
  • Submit any required documentation to support your request (e.g., medical certificates, proof of travel restrictions, etc.).

We will acknowledge your refund request within 48 hours and inform you of the next steps.

3. Cancellation Fees and Charges

Our cancellation fees are based on the date of cancellation relative to your departure date. The following applies:

A. Individual Bookings

  • More than 60 days before departure: Full refund minus a processing fee (typically 10-15% of the total booking cost).
  • 30-60 days before departure: 50% refund of the total booking cost.
  • Less than 30 days before departure: No refund available, except in exceptional circumstances (e.g., illness, travel restrictions).

B. Group Bookings

  • More than 90 days before departure: Full refund minus a processing fee.
  • 60-90 days before departure: 50% refund of the total group cost.
  • 30-60 days before departure: 25% refund of the total group cost.
  • Less than 30 days before departure: No refund.

Note: Group cancellations that affect the minimum number of travelers may lead to the cancellation of the entire group booking, and the above fees will apply.

C. Special Offers or Discounts

Refunds on special promotional fares or discounted tours may not be possible or may be subject to specific terms based on the promotion or discount applied.

4. Non-Refundable Deposits

In some cases, a non-refundable deposit may be required to confirm your booking. This deposit amount will be clearly stated in the booking confirmation. This deposit is typically non-refundable unless:

  • The booking is canceled due to force majeure (e.g., natural disasters, political unrest, etc.).
  • Ndewedo Tours and Safari cancels the tour for reasons beyond your control.

5. Refund for Services Not Provided

If any part of your travel experience is not provided as outlined (e.g., accommodation, meals, transport) due to a failure on our part or a third-party service provider, you may be eligible for a partial refund or compensation. This will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

6. Refund Method

Refunds will generally be issued using the same payment method used for the original booking, unless otherwise agreed upon. Please allow up to 30 days for the processing and receipt of your refund.

7. Force Majeure

If your tour or safari is canceled or significantly altered due to circumstances beyond our control (e.g., natural disasters, pandemics, government travel restrictions, or other unforeseen events), no refund will be given, but you will be offered the option to reschedule or receive a travel credit for future bookings. Please refer to our Force Majeure Policy for more details.

8. Travel Insurance

We strongly recommend that all travelers purchase comprehensive travel insurance to cover unforeseen cancellations, medical emergencies, trip interruption, and other potential issues. Travel insurance may cover cancellations made for reasons beyond your control, such as illness or injury, travel delays, or unexpected events.

9. Changes to Refund Policy

Ndewedo Tours and Safari reserves the right to modify or update this refund policy at any time. Any changes will be posted on our website with an updated effective date.

10. Contact Us

If you have any questions regarding this Refund Policy or would like to request a refund, please contact us:

Ndewedo Tours and Safari
📧 Email: info@ndewedotours.com
📞 Phone: +255 753 243 280
🌐 Website: https://ndewedotours.com/
📍 Office Address: Sakina Arusha P.O.BOX 11677

item.title: 6 Days : Kilimanjaro Climb via Marangu Route
item.dc:creator: anthonia

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: The 6 day Marangu Route ascent is the oldest route on Mount Kilimanjaro, also known as the Tourist Route or Coca Cola Route. You may have heard that out of all the routes up Mt. Kilimanjaro, the Marangu route is the easiest, cheapest and by far the most popular route for Kilimanjaro Climbing.

We will send a driver to the airport to pick you up and take you to the hotel in Arusha. Orientation will take place at the hotel. Our guides will highlight all the important details regarding your trek and an inspection of your trekking gear will take place.

You will have a chance to familiarize yourself with your guides, chefs and porters before departing the hotel in Arusha. You will begin your journey to the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro after completing the gate registration. A great length of the hike is spent venturing on a narrow trail that is enclosed by the evergreen rain forest. Reaching Kisambioni is a milestone as it signifies that we are at the halfway point of the trek. We will sit down and enjoy a picnic lunch. We will continue walking through the rain forests of Kilimanjaro after lunch. Our final destination is the Mandara Hut. Once we arrive you can decide whether you want to relax for the rest of the day or take a leisurely stroll to the Maundi Crater. If you face the northwest you will see the striking Mawenzi Peak which resembles a crown in the sky with its prickly edges. Turn to the east and you will see the picturesque landscapes of Taveta. Visiting on a day with clear skies will ensure that you get maximum viewing pleasure. You will spend the night in the A-frame Mandara Huts which accommodate up to seventy people and feature beds with mattresses. There are several sleeping huts and a dining area.

We will start heading towards Horombo Hut after breakfast. The environment will shift drastically as the Marangu Route requires us to travel through Mount Kilimanjaro’s moorland, a rock-strewn desert plain with succulent plants. There will be a picnic lunch at Kambi ya Taabu during the hike. If the skies are clear you will have a chance to witness the scenic views of the Mawenzi and Kibo peaks. We will arrive at the Horombo Huts at approximately 3:00 pm and the afternoon can be spent relaxing. The Horombo Huts are exceptionally busy but they’re considered to be the finest huts on Mount Kilimanjaro. The little, A-frame huts can house a maximum of eight people and provide suitable lodging for hikers ascending, descending and acclimation. They can accommodate a maximum of 120 hikers with additional room for porters, chiefs and guides.

After breakfast we will hike through the moorland and the alpine desert region of Mount Kilimanjaro. After hiking for about an hour we will encounter a small mountain stream called the Maua River. Once you pass Maua you will notice that the terrain gets smoother and the vegetation starts to diminish. We will have an appetizing lunch at the Middle Red Hill. We will continue our trek shortly after lunch and spend the next tour hours traveling to Kibo on a steady incline through Mount Kilimanjaro’s Saddle. The silver lining to traveling through a baron dessert is the breathtakingly stunning vista of the Kibo and Mawenzi peaks. You will reach the Kibo hut in the afternoon. It is recommended that you rest and prepare for your midnight climb.
Kibo Hut to Summit to Horombo Hut

The final leg of your journey is the ascent to Uhuru Peak which has been award the title The Roof of Africa. We will leave shortly after midnight and begin with the strenuous five hour hike to Gillman’s Point on the crater rim. This is considered to be the least challenging of the three crater ascent paths but it is still an arduous hike. William’s Point is the first major rest stop and it usually takes two hours from the Kibo Hut to arrive at the five thousand meter mark. After thirty minutes of hiking you will reach the rocky bends and twists that continue for over six hundred meters or until you reach Gillman’s Point. The incline from Gilman’s Point to Uhuru Peak increases gradually consequently it is not a difficult hike. You will feel tired and this part will take long due to the high altitude. The crater rim hike will last about two hours. Once you reach the summit, we have allocated time for you to take some photographs and celebrate your triumph. We will start descending to Horombo Hut – our final stop on the route. The route down the summit has magnificent views that you could not see when you were climbing the mountain. You will have a chance to stop at the Kibo Hut to recollect yourself and enjoy some energy dense snacks. We will reach the Horombo Huts in the afternoon and you can spend the time enjoying your last moments on the mountain.

We will finish the trek by descending to the Marangu Gate after breakfast. The final hike is simply magical. You will hike amid the gods in Mount Kilimanjaro’s tranquil cloud forest. We advise that you watch your step as the trail can be fairly slippery. Our vehicles will be waiting at Marangu Gate to drive you back to Arusha. You will have an opportunity to buy sodas and souvenirs to prove that the Marangu Route was conquered. Then, you can extend your Tanzania stay with the witnessing of our Big 5, found in Tanzania National Parks for Wildlife Safari.

item.title: 7 Days : Kilimanjaro Climb via Rongai Route
item.dc:creator: anthonia

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: The climb through the summit; Rongai Route is the only route that approaches Kilimanjaro from the north, near the Kenyan border. Rongai is the only route where climbers can watch wildlife in the first few days!

After completing the necessary registration formalities at Marangu National Park gate, we transfer by Landrover to Rongai. The climb begins from Nale Moru (1,950 m) on a small path that winds through fields of maize and potatoes before entering pine forest. The track then starts to climb consistently, but gently through attractive forest that shelters a variety of wildlife, including the beautiful Kilimanjaro Colobus monkey. These monkeys are black with a long ‘cape’ of white hair and a flowing white tail. The forest begins to thin out and the first camp is at the edge of the moorland zone, Rongai One Camp (2,600 m) with extensive views over the Kenyan plains. (3-4 hours walking).
Kibo And The Eastern Icefields On The Crater Rim

This is only a morning walk up to the campsite at ‘Second Cave’ (3,450 m). The walk is a steady ascent with superb views of Kibo and the Eastern icefields on the crater rim. The afternoon can be spend enjoying the view over the Kenyan plains or doing a short acclimatisation walk up towards Third Cave. (3-4 hours walking)

We now leave the main trail and strike out across the moorland on a smaller path towards the jagged peaks of Mawenzi. Our campsite is in a sheltered valley with giant senecios near Kikelewa Caves (3.600 m) After lunch, there is time to explore the valley or to rest. (3-4 hours walking).
The Next Camp At Mawenzi Tarn (4,330m)

A short but steep climb is rewarded by superb all round views and a tangible sense of wilderness. We leave vegetation behind shortly before reaching the next camp at Mawenzi Tarn (4,330m), spectacularly situated in a cirque directly beneath the towering spires of Mawenzi. The afternoon will be free to rest or explore the surrounding area as an aid to acclimatization. (3-4 hours walking)

We cross the lunar desert of the ‘Saddle’ between Mawenzi and Kibo to reach Kibo campsite (4,700m) at the bottom of the Kibo crater wall. The remainder of the day is spent resting in preparation for the final ascent before a very early night! (5-6 hours walking)
Crater rim at Gillman’s Point (5,685 m)

We will start the final, and by far the steepest and most demanding, part of the climb by torchlight around 1 a.m. We plod very slowly in the darkness on a switchback trail through loose volcanic scree to reach the crater rim at Gillman’s Point (5,685 m) We will rest there for a short time to enjoy the spectacular sunrise over Mawenzi. Those who are still feeling strong can make the three hour round trip to Uhuru Peak (5,896 m), passing close to the spectacular glaciers and ice cliffs that still occupy most of the summit area. The descent to Kibo (4,700 m) is surprisingly fast and, after some refreshment, we continue the descent to reach our final campsite at Horombo (3,720 m). (11-15 hours walking)

A steady descent takes us down through moorland to Mandara Hut (2,700m), the first stopping place at the Marangu route. We then continue descending through lovely lush forest on a good path to the National Park gate at Marangu (1,830 m). (5-6 hours walking)

Embark on a 16-day private safari across Kenya, Tanzania, and Zanzibar, exploring iconic destinations like Masai Mara, Serengeti, and Ngorongoro Crater. Experience thrilling game drives, relaxing beach time in Zanzibar, and cultural tours of Stone Town and Prison Island. Includes accommodations, transportation, and professional guide services, with prices starting from $5,500.
Your safari guide will pick you up from the airport and transfer you to your hotel 67for overnight

Your tour begins with a 7:30 am pick up from Ibis Styles and the drive to Masai Mara. This trip will take approximately 5 to 6.5 hours with a scenic stop at the Great Rift Valley. You will arrive in Masai Mara shortly after midday and check in at Enkorok Mara/camp, enjoy a hot lunch and then depart for an afternoon game drive. After the game drive, we will return to the lodge/camp to arrive around 6:00 pm, freshen up and enjoy a freshly prepared dinner. We will spend the night at Enkorok Mara Camp.

Today's itinerary is flexible and you can talk to your guide the night before and plan today's program. After breakfast, head out with your packed lunch and return to camp in the afternoon around 4:00 pm. Or you can depart at 6:00 am on a morning game drive (this is the best time to see the animals and a good chance to witness the hunt/kill). Later, return to the lodge for breakfast and some relaxation and head out on an afternoon game drive with packed lunch. You will stop at a picnic spot for packed lunch and then head out on a game drive until the park is closed. Around 6:00 pm you will return to Enkorok for dinner and overnight
Masai Mara to Lake Nakuru approx. 4 to 5 hours
Depart Masai Mara and head to Lake Nakuru. Arrive in time for lunch and afternoon game drive, dinner and overnight in Sopa forests
Early morning departure after breakfast and drive through Nairobi to the Amboseli National Park. Lunch at Sentrim Camp, Amboseli afternoon game drive and return to camp.
You can go on a full day game drive in Amboseli. Dinner and overnight at Sentrim Amboseli

We will depart after breakfast and be dropped off at the border Tanzanian side itinerary You will meet a Tanzanian driver at the border, ready to take you to the hotel where you will spend the night at the Pazuri Inn lodge

We will depart Arusha in the morning at 8:30 am and travel to Tarangire National Park, where you can marvel at the colossal termite mounds and ancient baobab trees. The picturesque landscape and diverse bird life help create the peaceful atmosphere of Tarangire National Park. The large elephant population is an extremely remarkable sight. African elephants are the largest land mammal and adult males can weigh up to seven tons. Tarangire's diverse wildlife includes lions, giraffes, warthogs, ostriches, impalas, cheetahs, mongooses, buffalos and baboons. When your safari is over, we will drive you to Bougainville lodge.. Here you will spend the night having dinner and you will have enough space to do body exercises and swim in the pool.
Tarangire National Park to Serengeti National Park

After breakfast at 7:30 am, we will head to Serengeti National Park. We will take the scenic route to the Serengeti, which will allow us to travel close to the Ngorongoro Crater. There is a chance of spotting animals. The endless golden savannah with patches of colour created by vegetation and wildlife makes it easy to understand why the Serengeti is one of the Seven Natural Wonders of Africa. We will stop so you can enjoy your picnic lunch on a kopje (a small hill in a generally flat area). We will continue into the Serengeti for a leisurely game drive. Overnights at Suenos de Africa luxury camp

We will start the day in the central Serengeti where we will have lunch and game viewing. Wildlife in the Serengeti is extremely diverse with regular sightings of lions, leopards, elephants, cheetahs, buffalos, zebras, wildebeests, elands, wild dogs, gazelles, crocodiles, giraffes, zebras, monkeys, baboons, hippos, rhinos and antelopes. There are a few factors that will affect the game you see such as migration of the herds and the season. The various bird species consist of some migratory birds from the Eurasian region. After sunset we will drive back to camp where you will spend the night at the same hotel of origin.
Serengeti Ngorongoro and Pazuri Inn Lodge

We will depart for Ngorongoro early in the morning as it is a wonderful time for animal spotting. We will go on a game drive with a picnic lunch inside the crater. Most animals tend to reside inside the crater due to its elevated structure. There is a good chance of seeing all members of “The Big 5”. The group is made up of some of Africa’s strongest animals – the ferocious lion, the giant elephant, the speedy leopard, the tough rhino and the buffalo. The crater was formed millions of years ago when a large volcano erupted. You can expect to encounter zebras, hippos, wildebeest and cackling hyenas. There are graceful flamingos along Soda Lake and vultures are constantly circling the sky looking for abandoned car bodies. Storks and geese are popular waterfowl in the crater. Our safari will end shortly after lunch. Our driver will make his way back to the hotel at Pazuri Inn. Overnight and dinner.

After breakfast, your office driver will come to pick you up based on your flight boarding time. Upon arrival at Abeid Amani Karume International Airport, you will be transferred to your chosen hotel or resort in Zanzibar. Spend the rest of the day relaxing and unwinding after your journey, perhaps enjoying the serene beaches or exploring the local area at your own pace. In the evening, consider dining at a seaside restaurant to enjoy the stunning views of the Indian Ocean.
Mnemba Island, Aquarium and Sunset Cruise

Start with an exciting excursion to Mnemba Island, where you’ll experience some of the best snorkeling in the Indian Ocean. The island’s pristine coral reefs and vibrant marine life provide a perfect setting for underwater exploration. Next, you’ll visit the Nungwi Natural Aquarium, where you can interact with sea turtles and learn about conservation efforts. As the day draws to a close, you’ll embark on a traditional Swahili dhow for a relaxing sunset cruise, enjoying drinks and snacks as you watch the sun set on the horizon.
Stone Town, Prison and Underwater Tour

You will start with a tour of Stone Town, a historic district known for its winding streets and rich cultural heritage. Key sites include the House of Wonders, the Old Fort and the Freddie Mercury Museum. After exploring Stone Town, you will take a boat ride to Prison Island, also known as Changuu Island. Here, you will visit a sanctuary for giant tortoises and learn about the island's fascinating history. Later, you will embark on an underwater tour, where you will descend into the depths to see the vibrant marine life and colorful coral reefs of Zanzibar's underwater world.
This day you will have a full day of relaxation after a long journey of different excursions
You will have free time to relax and shop for souvenirs before your transfer to the airport for departure
Transport in off-road vehicles ideal for game viewing and photography
All park entrance fees including government taxes
Service of a professional English-speaking driver/guide
All game drives detailed in the itinerary
Bottled mineral water during the safari
Domestic flight from Arusha to Zanzibar

item.title: 3 Days : Lake Manyara, Ngorongoro Crater & Tarangire Park Safari
item.dc:creator: anthonia
item.excerpt:encoded: Lake Manyara, Ngorongoro Crater & Tarangire Park Safari

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Experience a 3-day safari exploring Lake Manyara, Ngorongoro Crater, and Tarangire National Park. Discover diverse wildlife, from elephants and flamingos at Lake Manyara to the dense game population in Ngorongoro Crater and Tarangire’s giant baobab trees. This short yet intense safari offers an unforgettable glimpse into Tanzania’s most iconic wildlife regions.

Meet our professional tours guide/driver in Arusha town, who will deliver a short safari info briefing, after which, we travel to the Lake Manyara National Park. We arrive in time for lunch at the lodge. After lunch we head into the Lake Manyara National Park. This impressive park is one of Tanzania’s most dramatically located wildlife areas, consisting of a massive but shallow soda lake (covering two-thirds of the park) at the foot of the Great Rift Valley’s western escarpment. The park’s varied habitat attracts a wide variety of animals, including one of Africa’s largest concentrations of elephants, Manyara’s famous tree-climbing lions, as well as large flocks of flamingos attracted by the algae in the lake. Dinner and overnight at Marera valley lodge.
Distance: 130 km

After breakfast we descend 600m into this magnificent crater for a morning, half-day game drive. The Ngorongoro Crater is one of the most densely crowded African wildlife areas in the world and is home to an estimated 30,000 animals including some of Tanzania’s last remaining black rhino. Supported by a year round water supply and fodder, the Ngorongoro Crater supports a vast variety of animals, which include herds of wildebeest, zebra, buffalo, eland, warthog, hippo, and giant African elephants. Another big draw card to this picturesque national park is it’s dense population of predators, which include lions, hyenas, jackals, cheetahs and the ever-elusive leopard, which sometimes requires a trained eye to spot. We will enjoy a picnic lunch in the crater, after which we travel to the Tarangire National Park. Dinner and overnight at Mawemawe lodge Distance: 60km & 155 km

After breakfast do we head into the Tarangire National Park for a morning game drive. The park runs along the line of the Tarangire River and is mainly made up of low-lying hills on the Great Rift Valley floor. Its natural vegetation mainly consists of Acacia woodland and giant African Baobab trees, with huge swamp areas in the south. Both the river and the swamps act like a magnet for wild animals, during Tanzania’s dry season. The Tarangire National Park is reputed to contain some of the largest elephant herds in Africa. This African national park is also home to three rare species of animals – the Greater Kudu, the Fringed-eared Oryx, as well as a few Ashy Starlings. We return to the lodge for lunch after which we will depart for Arusha town and we will end our African safari adventure. The group should tip the tour guide around $20 a day for all our safaris. You will be taken to your hotel, which ends our safari packages services. Non game-viewing travel time: 2 hours Distance: 120 km
